The smoothing operator \(\mathcal{F}\) maps raw weather inputs to a reduced set of scenarios \(\mathcal{S}_{\text{analytical}}\), preserving temporal coherence. Each scenario is evaluated by a decision rule \(\mathcal{D}\) to determine flight impacts. Finally, these outcomes are aggregated using probability weighting \(\mathbb{P}\) to compute overall disruption likelihood. This process exhibits a dual structure: probabilistic forecasting (GSI) and deterministic action (GSE). Failure modes include loss of temporal smoothness in \(\mathcal{F}\), inconsistency in \(\mathcal{R}\), and incorrect probability assignment in \(\mathbb{P}\).
